uncited: This method tracks which finest-level brick cells have been visited by rays to enable selective streaming and refinement, preventing redundant data transfers when multiple rays share a cell.
It differs from its parent [XBrickMap](3116-xbrickmap.md) by adding a runtime occupancy buffer that complements the static hierarchical skipping with dynamic visitation history.
*   **Input:** Brick index `c` (converted to `vec3u`), grid dimensions `grid` (from indirection texture), and the current `rayVisited` atomic buffer.
The `rayVisited` buffer is a storage buffer of type `array<atomic<u32>>`.
Cell index `i` corresponds to bit `i & 31` of word `1 + (i >> 5)`.
A single-word buffer disables the feature.
**Atomic Check and Set:** Perform an atomic read-modify-write.
*   **Buffer Size:** Must accommodate all finest-level bricks.
*   **ISO Gradient Sampling:** Gradient calculations may sample cells outside the volume (e.g., beyond clip planes).
These cells must be marked as visited to remain eligible for refinement.
*   **Time Complexity:** $O(1)$ per brick visit for the atomic operation.
*   **Memory Complexity:** $O(N/32)$ words for $N$ bricks, plus 1 unused word.
*   **When to use:** When multiple rays share cells and streaming overhead is significant.
*   **When not:** When memory bandwidth is the primary bottleneck and atomic contention is high.
This technique is part of the Kiln renderer, a WebGPU-native out-of-core volume rendering system for multi-GB datasets.
It was presented in an unofficial GitHub repository in 2026.
